question: Does the P0590 improvement require a nonzero return radius—evidence for an arc/return morphology—or is ordinary baryon-map smoothing sufficient?

disclosed_P0590_result.reason_for_audit: A ring whose width equals its radius has substantial central support and can mimic a Gaussian smoothing kernel.

families.strict_arc_return: return radius at least 8 arcsec and width no more than half the return radius

selection: Lock the best member of each family by mean development-map JSD, then transfer all three unchanged to the same Bradac and Williams method holdouts.
claim_limits: This audit reuses all four already opened MACS J0416 model maps and is a diagnostic, not a new holdout.
A nonzero ring outperforming a Gaussian would establish morphological necessity only; it would not show that gravity traveled through a hidden coordinate.
If Gaussian smoothing is competitive, P0590 cannot be cited as evidence for arcing gravity even if it fits far better than the unsmoothed baryon map.
